units.title: Forces
units.summary: This unit focuses on quantifying and comparing energy transfers in different processes, such as motion changes, electrical circuits, and fuel burning. It examines forces as interactions between objects, using diagrams and measurements, including contact and non-contact forces.
units.whyThisWhyNow: Building on pupils’ prior knowledge of forces, including simple machines, where they explored resistance forces such as air and water resistance and friction, this unit deepens their understanding by introducing forces as interactions between objects, including contact and non-contact forces, using diagrams and measurements. This ensures that pupils can contextualise how forces affect motion before they progress to the next unit, Hidden forces, where they will explore more complex concepts like turning forces, forces that hold objects on surfaces, and buoyancy.

lessons.title: What forces do
lessons.outcome: I can describe what forces are and what forces do.

lessons.title: The different kinds of force
lessons.outcome: I can identify and describe different kinds of force and their effects.

lessons.title: Measuring forces
lessons.outcome: I can use newton meters to measure forces accurately.

lessons.title: Using force arrows
lessons.outcome: I can draw and label force arrows to accurately represent forces acting.

lessons.title: Balanced and unbalanced forces
lessons.outcome: I can use the idea of resultant force to explain whether a change of speed occurs or not.

lessons.title: Friction
lessons.outcome: I can describe the characteristics of friction forces, explain what causes friction and describe how friction can be reduced.

lessons.title: Reducing friction: practical
lessons.outcome: I can collect data to test the effectiveness of different lubricants, taking steps to ensure a fair test.

lessons.title: Reducing friction: analysis
lessons.outcome: I can analyse data from an investigation to test the effectiveness of different lubricants.

lessons.title: Energy
lessons.outcome: I can identify different energy stores that objects have and explain why they have each energy store.

lessons.title: Transferring energy
lessons.outcome: I can identify when stores of energy change, and describe causes of energy transfer between stores.

units.title: Solid, liquid, gas states and changes of state
units.topic: Y7.02 · Solid, liquid, gas states and changes of state (Chemistry)
units.summary: This unit covers the properties of solids, liquids, and gases using the particle model, including gas pressure. It explains changes of state in terms of the particle model while developing skills in using appropriate techniques, apparatus, and materials in lab work.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Introduction to states of matter and changing states, where they explored how solids, liquids, and gases change when heated or cooled. It develops their understanding of the particle model, focusing on how particles behave and interact during changes of state, including gas pressure and motion. This positions pupils to deepen their knowledge in the next unit, Solutions, where they will apply these concepts to understand the behaviour of mixtures and how they can be separated, further reinforcing the thread of substance interactions.

lessons.title: Solid and liquid states
lessons.outcome: I can describe the properties of substances that are in the solid and liquid states.

lessons.title: Melting: particle model
lessons.outcome: I can use the particle model to explain why substances have different melting points, and use a thermometer to measure melting points.

lessons.title: Bunsen burners
lessons.outcome: I can light a Bunsen burner safely and control the temperature of the flame.

lessons.title: Melting: melting points and freezing points
lessons.outcome: I can measure the melting point and freezing point of a substance.

lessons.title: Particle model of substances in the gas state
lessons.outcome: I can describe how the arrangement and movement of particles alters when a substance changes from the liquid to gas state.

lessons.title: Boiling and condensing
lessons.outcome: I can measure the boiling point of water and explain what happens to particles when a substance in the gas state condenses.

lessons.title: Changes of state: energy and evaporation
lessons.outcome: I can describe and explain what happens when a substance changes state and how evaporation occurs.

units.title: Cells
units.summary: This unit explores cell structures, their functions, and differences between plant and animal cells. It includes adaptations of unicellular organisms and the organisation of multicellular organisms. Skills in using safe techniques, recording data, and evaluating methods in lab work are developed.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Living things and where they live, where they explored basic biological structures and how organisms are adapted to their environments. It develops their understanding by focusing on the structure and function of cells, the building blocks of all living things, including specialised cell functions. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Human skeleton and muscles, where they will apply their knowledge of cells to understand the organisation of tissues, organs, and systems, highlighting how cellular structures contribute to movement and support.

lessons.title: The common processes of all living organisms
lessons.outcome: I can describe processes that happen in all living organisms.

lessons.title: Observing cells with a light microscope
lessons.outcome: I can use a light microscope to observe cells.

lessons.title: Preparing and observing a microscope slide
lessons.outcome: I can prepare a microscope slide with a specimen of tissue, observe it using a microscope, and record my observations in a scientific line drawing.

lessons.title: Animal cell structures and their functions
lessons.outcome: I can identify common structures of animal cells and describe what these structures do.

lessons.title: Plant cell structures and their functions
lessons.outcome: I can identify common structures of plant cells and describe what these structures do.

lessons.title: Multicellular and unicellular organisms
lessons.outcome: I can explain the differences between multicellular and unicellular organisms.

lessons.title: Specialised cells are adapted for their functions
lessons.outcome: I can describe how specialised cells in animals and plants are adapted for specific functions.

units.title: Our solar system and beyond
units.topic: Y7.04 · Our solar system and beyond (Physics)
units.summary: This unit explores gravity as the force between masses, including weight calculation using gravitational field strength. It covers the relationship between Earth, the Moon, and the Sun, the concept of light years, and seasonal changes due to Earth’s tilt.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Earth, Sun and Moon, where they explored the movement and interactions of these celestial bodies. It expands their understanding by examining the solar system, including the concept of gravity as a force between masses and the role of gravity in maintaining orbital paths. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Gravity in space, where they will delve deeper into the effects of gravity on orbits, the formation of celestial bodies, and evidence supporting theories about the universe's expansion.

lessons.title: The spinning Earth
lessons.outcome: I can describe the motions of Earth to explain day, night and a year, and describe the motion of the Moon to explain why it appears to change shape.

lessons.title: Our solar system
lessons.outcome: I can describe our solar system, including ideas about the locations, movements, sizes and distances of the different objects within our solar system.

lessons.title: Gravity
lessons.outcome: I can describe the effects of gravity acting towards the centre of a nearby planet, moon or star.

lessons.title: Stars, galaxies and the universe
lessons.outcome: I can describe what stars and galaxies are and explain how they look when seen from Earth.

lessons.title: Heating by the Sun
lessons.outcome: I can explain why the heating effect of the Sun is greater at midday than at sunrise.

lessons.title: Earth's tilt
lessons.outcome: I can explain why it is winter in the southern hemisphere when it is summer in the northern hemisphere.

lessons.title: Seasons on Earth
lessons.outcome: I can explain how and why the seasons change, and why some countries do not have summers and winters.

lessons.title: Changing ideas about Earth
lessons.outcome: I can describe how and why our understanding of the position and motion of Earth has changed over time.

units.title: Solutions
units.summary: This unit explores the concepts of pure substances, mixtures, and diffusion in liquids and gases. It emphasises accuracy, precision, and the use of appropriate techniques during investigations. The focus is on making predictions and recording reliable observations.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Solid, liquid, gas states and changes of state, where they explored how particles behave in different states and change under various conditions. It advances their knowledge by investigating how substances mix to form solutions and the factors that affect solubility. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Separation techniques, where they will apply their understanding of mixtures and solutions to learn how substances can be separated, deepening their grasp of the interactions and properties of materials.

lessons.title: Pure substances
lessons.outcome: I can describe the difference between a pure substance and a mixture.

lessons.title: Mixtures: choosing equipment
lessons.outcome: I can identify and name common laboratory equipment that are useful for when working with mixtures.

lessons.title: Mixtures: equipment diagrams
lessons.outcome: I can create scientific diagrams of common laboratory equipment, showing how they are used together.

lessons.title: Mixtures and solutions
lessons.outcome: I can use key terms to describe a solution and describe how making a solution affects its total mass.

lessons.title: Diffusion
lessons.outcome: I can explain how particles spread through a fluid.

lessons.title: Dissolving
lessons.outcome: I can use the particle model to explain both how solutions form and how solutions differ from a suspension.

lessons.title: Variables
lessons.outcome: I can identify independent, dependent, and control variables and describe the differences between them.

lessons.title: Dissolving: scientific methods
lessons.outcome: I can identify features of a good method and use them to improve a method that will investigate dissolving.

lessons.title: Solubility: practical
lessons.outcome: I can carry out a fair test to investigate solubility and record the measurements in an appropriate table of results.

lessons.title: Solubility: analysis
lessons.outcome: I can draw an appropriate representation of solubility data and use it to write a conclusion.

lessons.title: Saturated solutions
lessons.outcome: I can compare data involving the solubility of different solutes and use it to describe saturation.

units.title: Ecosystems
units.summary: This unit explores the interdependence of organisms in ecosystems, including food webs and insect-pollinated crops. It examines how organisms interact with their environment and the impact of toxic materials. It also highlights the importance of biodiversity and preserving genetic material.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from More about food chains, where they explored the flow of energy through organisms as they interact in ecosystems. It deepens their understanding by examining the complex interdependence of organisms, the impact of environmental changes, and the importance of biodiversity. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Biodiversity, where they will further explore how species interactions and environmental factors influence the survival and adaptation of organisms, reinforcing the thread of ecosystem dynamics and conservation.

lessons.title: Food chains
lessons.outcome: I can identify producers and consumers and explain what is shown by a food chain diagram.

lessons.title: Predator-prey relationships
lessons.outcome: I can describe and explain the relationship between predator and prey populations.

lessons.title: Adaptations of predators and prey
lessons.outcome: I can describe how predators and prey are adapted to help them survive.

lessons.title: Food webs
lessons.outcome: I can explain what is shown by a food web diagram and explain the effects that a change in the size of a population could have on other populations in the same community.

lessons.title: Ecosystems and habitats
lessons.outcome: I can describe what makes an ecosystem, can identify features of habitats and explain how organisms are adapted to live in their habitat.

lessons.title: Pollination and human food security
lessons.outcome: I can describe the importance of pollination for food production.

lessons.title: Using chemicals in farming
lessons.outcome: I can describe and explain the benefits and drawbacks of using chemicals such as fertilisers and pesticides in farming.

lessons.title: Bioaccumulation
lessons.outcome: I can describe how toxic materials can accumulate and affect organisms in a food chain.

lessons.title: The importance of biodiversity
lessons.outcome: I can explain why it is important to maintain biodiversity and suggest how we might do this.

units.title: Sound, light and vision
units.summary: This unit explores sound and light waves, including frequencies, echoes, reflection, absorption, and the need for a medium for sound to travel. It also compares light and matter waves, investigates light transmission and colour, and examines wave properties and effects.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Light and how it travels, where they explored the basic properties of light, including how it moves in straight lines and forms shadows. It extends this knowledge by examining the nature of sound and light waves, their interactions, and how they are perceived by the human senses. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Making images, where they will apply their understanding of wave properties to explore how light is used to create images, further enhancing their grasp of the role of waves in communication and perception.

lessons.title: Sound vibrations
lessons.outcome: I can describe how sounds are caused and explain what sets the volume and pitch of a sound.

lessons.title: Travelling vibrations

lessons.title: Travelling sound

lessons.title: Reflecting and absorbing sound
lessons.outcome: I can describe factors that affect how much sound a material or object might reflect or absorb, and explain ways to reduce noise.

lessons.title: Shadows
lessons.outcome: I can describe what happens when light travels and how shadows can form.

lessons.title: Reflecting light from mirrors
lessons.outcome: I can investigate the reflection of light from mirrors by tracing beams of light and measuring angles, and compare results to the known laws of reflection.

lessons.title: How we see things

lessons.title: Reflections in mirrors
lessons.outcome: I can explain why reflections (images) are seen in mirrors and describe the properties of mirror images.

units.title: Heredity and DNA
units.summary: This unit examines the transmission of genetic information through heredity, how scientific methods evolve with new evidence, the importance of publishing and peer review, and the Study of DNA, chromosomes, and genes while developing lab skills focusing on safety.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Evolution and inheritance, where they examined how genetic traits are passed through generations and how species adapt over time. It deepens their understanding by exploring the detailed mechanisms of heredity, including DNA, chromosomes, and genes, and how genetic information is transmitted. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Reproduction in humans, where they will apply their knowledge of genetic inheritance to understand human reproductive processes, focusing on the roles of genetic material in development and variation.

lessons.title: Heredity
lessons.outcome: I can describe what is meant by heredity and why offspring usually look similar to their parents.

lessons.title: Heredity and genetic material
lessons.outcome: I can explain that some, but not all, features are inherited when genetic material is passed from parents to their offspring.

lessons.title: Genetic material and DNA
lessons.outcome: I can describe what genetic material is and where it is stored in animals, plants and microorganisms.

lessons.title: A model of the structure of DNA
lessons.outcome: I can describe the structure of DNA and evaluate models of it.

lessons.title: DNA from fruit
lessons.outcome: I can observe DNA extracted from fruit and identify the main apparatus and steps in the extraction method.

lessons.title: The discovery of the structure of DNA
lessons.outcome: I can describe how scientists collected evidence and shared findings to develop a model to describe the structure of DNA.

lessons.title: DNA, chromosomes, genes and the genome
lessons.outcome: I can explain the difference between DNA, chromosomes, genes and the genome.

units.title: Separation techniques
units.summary: This unit covers techniques for separating mixtures, including filtration, evaporation, distillation, and chromatography, as well as identifying pure substances. Conduct experiments safely, record observations, evaluate methods, and suggest improvements.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Properties, changes and separating materials, where they explored material properties and methods of separation. It focuses on techniques like filtration, evaporation, and distillation to separate mixtures based on their properties. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Understanding chemical reactions, where they will apply this knowledge to explore how substances interact and change during chemical reactions, deepening their understanding of material behaviour.

lessons.title: Separating an insoluble solid from a liquid
lessons.outcome: I can use my understanding of the properties of solids and liquids to work out how to separate some mixtures.

lessons.title: Separating a soluble solid from a liquid
lessons.outcome: I can explain how dissolving can be reversed to separate a soluble solid from a liquid.

lessons.title: Separating pure salt from dirty rock salt
lessons.outcome: I can suggest how to combine separation techniques in order to separate pure salt from a sample of rock salt.

lessons.title: Separating liquids

lessons.title: Simple distillation

lessons.title: Distillation: practical

lessons.title: Chromatography
lessons.outcome: I can describe how chromatography works and use a chromatogram to answer questions about a substance.

units.title: Human skeleton and muscles
units.summary: This unit investigates the structure and functions of the human skeleton, including support, protection, movement, and blood cell production. Explore biomechanics, the interaction of muscles and the skeleton, and antagonistic muscles while measuring muscle force.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Cells, where they explored cell structures and functions as the basic units of life. It extends their understanding by examining how the human skeleton and muscles work together for support, protection, and movement. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Diffusion, where they will apply their knowledge of cellular functions to understand how substances move in and out of cells, highlighting the importance of these processes in body systems.

lessons.title: The human skeleton
lessons.outcome: I can describe the role of the human skeleton in support, protection and making blood cells.

lessons.title: Muscles
lessons.outcome: I can describe what muscles are made of and how they move.

lessons.title: Movement
lessons.outcome: I can explain how muscles work together to move bones at joints.

lessons.title: Biomechanics
lessons.outcome: I can calculate the moment of a force around a joint.

units.title: Heating and cooling
units.summary: This unit explains energy transfer between objects due to temperature differences, through conduction or radiation, the role of insulators, and thermal equilibrium. It covers particle arrangements and motions in solids, liquids, and gases and Brownian motion.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Solid, liquid, and gas states and changes of state, where they explored how particles behave in different states and respond to heating and cooling. It deepens their understanding by examining energy transfer, thermal equilibrium, and the role of insulators. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Particle explanations of density and pressure, where they will apply their knowledge of particle behaviour to explore how density and pressure are influenced by particle arrangement and movement.

lessons.title: Measuring temperature
lessons.outcome: I can safely and accurately measure the temperature of different objects using a thermometer.

lessons.title: Changing temperature
lessons.outcome: I can describe what happens to the particles that make up a solid or liquid when the temperature changes.

lessons.title: Mixing substances of different temperatures
lessons.outcome: I can predict the resulting temperature when two substances of different temperatures are put together.

lessons.title: Cooling

lessons.title: Thermal conductors
lessons.outcome: I can use the idea of vibrating particles to explain heating by thermal conduction.

lessons.title: Thermal insulators

lessons.title: Energy and temperature
lessons.outcome: I can describe the difference between the temperature and the energy of an object or substance.

lessons.title: Energy and substance
lessons.outcome: I can describe differences between the energy of different substances at the same temperature.

units.title: Diffusion
units.summary: This unit explores diffusion's role in material movement in and between cells and involves making predictions, observations and measurements with various methods.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Human skeleton and muscles, where they explored the structure and function of body systems. It deepens their understanding by examining diffusion as a key process for transporting substances in and between cells. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Human digestive system, where they will apply their knowledge of diffusion to understand how nutrients are absorbed into the bloodstream, highlighting the importance of these processes in digestion and overall body function.

lessons.title: Diffusion: moving particles
lessons.outcome: I can explain that diffusion is the movement of particles of a substance from an area of higher to lower concentration.

lessons.title: Diffusion through a permeable material: practical
lessons.outcome: I can explain observations of diffusion through jelly cubes (a permeable material).

lessons.title: Diffusion through the cell membrane

lessons.title: Diffusion through a selectively-permeable membrane: practical
lessons.outcome: I can explain observations of diffusion through a selectively-permeable membrane.

units.title: Climate change and living sustainably
units.topic: Y7.13 · Climate change and living sustainably (Biology)
units.summary: This unit introduces the greenhouse effect, global warming and the impact of climate change on weather events. It explores some actions that can be taken to use resources, and to live, in a sustainable way.
units.whyThisWhyNow: The purpose of this unit is to give a brief introduction to the greenhouse effect, global warming and climate change using concrete ideas from topics covered through Y7 science lessons. It introduces pupils to evidence from climate science, to start addressing their questions about climate change in a clear, positive and relevant way. The key message is that climate change ‘is real, it’s us, it’s bad, there’s hope’. In the next climate change unit, the local actions considered here are used as stepping stones to understand how larger scale actions for tackling climate change can be delivered.

lessons.title: The greenhouse effect
lessons.outcome: I can explain what causes Earth's greenhouse effect and why it affects global temperature.

lessons.title: Global warming
lessons.outcome: I can describe evidence for global warming and how it is related to human activities.

lessons.title: Climate change and human activities
lessons.outcome: I can explain what is meant by climate change and how it is related to human activities.

lessons.title: Sustainable use of resources
lessons.outcome: I can explain what is meant by the sustainable use of resources, and describe ways to make transport and buildings more sustainable.

lessons.title: Eating sustainably
lessons.outcome: I can compare the impacts that different foods have on climate change and suggest ways to eat more sustainably.

lessons.title: Heating and cooling our school sustainably
lessons.outcome: I can describe ways to reduce the need for heating or cooling in a school.

lessons.title: Waste and recycling
lessons.outcome: I can explain how to use resources more sustainably and reduce waste.

units.title: Human digestive system
units.summary: This unit examines the human digestive system, including the roles of tissues, organs, enzymes, and beneficial bacteria. It also focuses on evaluating risks, interpreting data, identifying patterns, and suggesting improvements to enhance the reliability of investigations.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Diffusion, where they explored how substances move in and out of cells. It deepens their understanding by examining the human digestive system, focusing on how nutrients are broken down and absorbed through diffusion into the bloodstream. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Breathing and respiration, where they will apply their understanding of diffusion to explore gas exchange in the lungs, further connecting the role of diffusion in vital body processes.

lessons.title: The parts of the human digestive system
lessons.outcome: I can describe parts of the digestive system and how they are adapted to digest food.

lessons.title: Digestion and enzymes
lessons.outcome: I can describe the processes of mechanical and chemical digestion that break down food to release nutrients, including the role of enzymes.

lessons.title: Food tests: practical
lessons.outcome: I can carry out tests for nutrients and some of the substances they are broken down into.

lessons.title: Bacteria in the human digestive system
lessons.outcome: I can describe the important roles of bacteria in the human digestive system.

lessons.title: Absorption and transport of nutrients in humans
lessons.outcome: I can describe how the digestive system and circulatory system work together to absorb nutrients and transport them around the body.

units.title: Atoms, elements and compounds
units.summary: This unit explores the basic atomic model, the differences between atoms, elements, and compounds, and the varying physical and chemical properties of elements. It covers chemical symbols, formulae, SI units, and IUPAC nomenclature, emphasising their use in describing elements and compounds.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Solid, liquid, gas states and changes of state, where they explored particle behaviour in different states and how materials change under various conditions. It enhances their understanding by focusing on the structure of atoms, elements, and compounds, and how these fundamental particles combine. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Understanding chemical reactions, where they will apply this knowledge to explore how atoms rearrange during chemical reactions, reinforcing the principles of matter and its transformations.

lessons.title: Atoms and elements
lessons.outcome: I can describe what a chemical element is and give some examples.

lessons.title: Properties of elements
lessons.outcome: I can describe the chemical and physical properties of different chemical elements.

lessons.title: Metallic elements
lessons.outcome: I can describe the properties of metal elements and compare them to non-metal elements.

lessons.title: Molecular elements
lessons.outcome: I can describe a molecule and draw pictures of elements made from molecules.

lessons.title: Common elements
lessons.outcome: I can communicate clearly some properties, uses and dangers of one or two common elements.

lessons.title: Compounds and their formation
lessons.outcome: I can explain the difference between a compound and an element.

lessons.title: Chemical formulae
lessons.outcome: I can use chemical symbols to write down chemical formulae for elements and compounds.

lessons.title: Naming compounds
lessons.outcome: I can name compounds from their chemical formulae.

lessons.title: A particle model of chemical reactions
lessons.outcome: I can draw particles diagrams of reactants and products to show how they are rearranged by a chemical reaction.

units.title: Biodiversity
units.summary: This unit examines environmental changes and their impact on species' survival and adaptation, potentially leading to extinction. It also develops skills for interpreting data and observations, evaluating errors, and using SI units and IUPAC chemical nomenclature in scientific contexts.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Ecosystems, where they examined the interdependence of organisms and the impact of environmental changes. It deepens their understanding by focusing on biodiversity, exploring the variety of life forms and their roles within ecosystems. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Living organisms and their environments, where they will apply this knowledge to study how biotic and abiotic factors influence the distribution and survival of species, reinforcing the importance of maintaining biodiversity.

lessons.title: Interdependence within ecosystems
lessons.outcome: I can describe ways in which organisms are interdependent within ecosystems.

lessons.title: Pyramids of number
lessons.outcome: I can create and interpret pyramids of number to show the size of a population at each trophic level.

lessons.title: Pyramids of biomass
lessons.outcome: I can create and interpret pyramids of biomass.

lessons.title: Plants are adapted for their environment
lessons.outcome: I can describe how some plants are adapted to help them survive, and how environmental conditions affect plant biodiversity positively and negatively.

lessons.title: Animals are adapted for their environment
lessons.outcome: I can describe how some animals are adapted to help them survive, and how environmental conditions affect animal biodiversity.

lessons.title: Ecological sampling of living organisms
lessons.outcome: I can describe and choose suitable methods to sample populations of plants or animals.

lessons.title: Ecological sampling using a quadrat
lessons.outcome: I can use a quadrat to sample populations of organisms.

lessons.title: Conserving biodiversity
lessons.outcome: I can describe a number of ways in which humans are impacting on biodiversity.

units.title: Understanding chemical reactions
units.summary: This unit covers the conservation of mass in changes of state and chemical reactions, including atom rearrangement. It also focuses on representing reactions with formulae and equations, exploring combustion, decomposition, and displacement, and distinguishing chemical from physical changes.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Atoms, elements and compounds, where they explored the basic building blocks of matter and how elements combine. It deepens their understanding by examining chemical reactions, focusing on how atoms rearrange to form new substances. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Acids and bases, where they will apply this knowledge to explore specific reactions, such as neutralisation, reinforcing their understanding of how substances interact chemically.

lessons.title: Characteristics of chemical reactions
lessons.outcome: I can describe some of the changes that indicate a chemical reaction is taking place.

lessons.title: Conservation of mass and balanced symbol equations
lessons.outcome: I can explain the conservation of mass and write balanced chemical equations to show how the atoms of reactants in a chemical reaction are rearranged to form products.

lessons.title: Chemical reactions: oxidation
lessons.outcome: I can describe oxidation reactions, including combustion and rusting, and name the products of some oxidation reactions.

lessons.title: Chemical reactions: combustion
lessons.outcome: I can describe the processes of combustion and burning, and name the products of these reactions.

lessons.title: Chemical reactions: decomposition
lessons.outcome: I can describe what happens during decomposition reactions, and write chemical equations to show these.

lessons.title: Chemical reactions: precipitation
lessons.outcome: I can describe what happens during precipitation reactions, and write chemical equations to show these.

units.title: Moving by force
units.summary: This unit explores speed, forces, and motion, including effects on objects. It covers deriving equations, calculations, and distance-time graphs. Learn to use force arrows, identify balanced and unbalanced forces, and understand their impact on movement.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Forces, where they explored different types of forces and how they affect motion. It deepens their understanding by examining how forces cause objects to move, stop, and change direction, using force diagrams and calculations. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Measuring and calculating motion, where they will apply their knowledge of forces to quantify motion through speed, velocity, and acceleration, enhancing their grasp of the principles governing movement.

lessons.title: Calculating speed
lessons.outcome: I can calculate speed.

lessons.outcome: I can accurately measure the average speed of a trolley moving down a ramp.

lessons.title: Reading distance-time graphs

lessons.title: Changing speed
