lessons.title: Streamlining
lessons.outcome: I can explain how streamlining reduces drag.

lessons.title: Comparing the speeds of different parachutes
lessons.outcome: I can explain how the size of a parachute affects its top speed.

lessons.title: Changing the speed of a parachute
lessons.outcome: I can clearly describe how drag forces affect the motion of falling objects.

units.title: Species and classification (differences between species)
units.topic: Y8.06 · Species and classification (differences between species) (Biology)
units.summary: This unit explores the differences between species and how to interpret observations and data to identify patterns and draw conclusions. It also focuses on making and recording observations using various methods, evaluating their reliability, and suggesting improvements for investigations.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Why we group and classify living things, where they explored the principles of classification and the characteristics that distinguish different groups. It deepens their understanding by examining the differences between species and how these distinctions inform classification. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Variation (differences within species), where they will explore how differences within a species contribute to diversity and adaptation, reinforcing the importance of classification in understanding biological variation.

lessons.title: Classification and species
lessons.outcome: I can explain how organisms are classified into groups, and what a species is.

lessons.title: Classifying organisms using a classification key
lessons.outcome: I can explain how to use a classification key, and the importance of classifying organisms into groups within larger groups.

lessons.title: Identification and classification in the field
lessons.outcome: I can use a classification key to identify and classify organisms in their natural habitats.

lessons.title: Classification at the cellular level
lessons.outcome: I can identify cell features that can be used to classify organisms into the kingdoms of animals, plants, fungi and bacteria.

units.title: Variation (differences within species)
units.summary: This unit examines variation within species, both continuous and discontinuous, using measurements and graphical representations. It also emphasises objectivity, accuracy, precision, and repeatability in investigations, the use of appropriate techniques, and the effective presentation of data.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Species and classification (differences between species), where they examined how species differ and the role of classification. It deepens their understanding by exploring variations within species, highlighting how individual differences contribute to diversity. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Adaptations, competition, natural selection and evolution, where they will apply their knowledge to understand how variation drives adaptation and evolution, shaping how species survive and thrive in their environments.

lessons.title: Reproduction and variation
lessons.outcome: I can explain why offspring look similar but not identical to their parents and one another.

lessons.title: Variation within species
lessons.outcome: I can describe examples of variation between individuals of the same species and explain what causes this variation.

lessons.title: Continuous and discontinuous variation: practical
lessons.outcome: I can describe and measure examples of discontinuous and continuous variation in features.

lessons.title: Discontinuous variation: data handling and analysis
lessons.outcome: I can plot data on discontinuous variation on a bar chart and suggest possible causes for the variation.

lessons.title: Continuous variation: data handling and analysis
lessons.outcome: I can plot data on continuous variation on a histogram and suggest possible causes for the variation.

units.title: Earth's resources
units.summary: This unit explores Earth's composition, structure, and rock cycle, including the formation of igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks. It also examines Earth as a source of limited resources and the importance of recycling, alongside skills in making and evaluating observations and measurements.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Rocks and soils, where they explored the formation and classification of rocks and the composition of soils. It deepens their understanding by examining Earth's resources, including how these materials are used and the importance of sustainable management. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Carbon cycle and climate change, where they will apply their knowledge to understand the role of Earth's resources in global cycles and the impact of human activity on climate, reinforcing the need for responsible resource use.

lessons.title: Inside rock
lessons.outcome: I can make detailed observations of different rocks and use key terms to describe features of them.

lessons.title: Rocks and minerals
lessons.outcome: I can describe differences between rocks and minerals.

lessons.title: Types of rocks
lessons.outcome: I can use features to classify rocks into different groups and suggest properties of each type.

lessons.title: Structure of Earth
lessons.outcome: I can describe the structure of Earth.

lessons.title: Tectonic plates
lessons.outcome: I can describe evidence of how we know tectonic plates move across the surface of Earth.

lessons.title: Igneous rock
lessons.outcome: I can explain how igneous rocks form and describe features of different types.

lessons.title: Metamorphic rock
lessons.outcome: I can describe how rock can be changed deep underground.

units.title: Series circuits
units.summary: This unit covers electric current, potential difference, and resistance in series and parallel circuits. It also explores charge separation, electron transfer, and electric fields. The unit focuses on interpreting data, identifying patterns, and drawing conclusions using scientific knowledge.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Changing circuits, where they explored the components and variations of electrical circuits and how changes affect circuit behaviour. It deepens their understanding by focusing on series circuits, exploring current, voltage, and resistance in a simple loop. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Magnets and electromagnets, where they will apply their knowledge of electric circuits to understand how electricity and magnetism interact, further enhancing their understanding of electromagnetic systems.

lessons.title: Making a series circuit
lessons.outcome: I can use a circuit diagram to build a series circuit and then draw a circuit diagram of a completed circuit.

lessons.title: Fixing faulty circuits
lessons.outcome: I can describe how to build a simple test circuit, use it to check for faulty components, and find faults in a conducting circuit loop.

lessons.title: Electric current
lessons.outcome: I can describe how a cell causes current in a circuit and explain the movement of electrons.

lessons.title: Measuring electric current
lessons.outcome: I can measure current and describe the rule for current in a series circuit.

lessons.title: Measuring voltage
lessons.outcome: I can describe how to measure voltage and the effect of different cell or battery voltages on an electric circuit.

lessons.title: Changing voltage
lessons.outcome: I can describe and apply the rules for voltage in a series circuit.

lessons.title: Static electricity
lessons.outcome: I can describe how objects with a positive or negative charge attract or repel other charged objects.

lessons.title: Static electricity: charge
lessons.outcome: I can describe what charges are and how they are transferred between some objects, giving them opposite charges.

units.title: Reproduction in humans
units.summary: This unit explores human reproduction, covering the structure and function of male and female reproductive systems, the menstrual cycle, gametes, fertilisation, gestation, and birth. It also examines how maternal lifestyle impacts the foetus through the placenta.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Heredity and DNA, where they explored genetic transmission and how DNA controls traits in living organisms. It deepens their understanding by examining human reproduction, focusing on the structure and function of reproductive systems and the role of genetics in inheritance. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Reproduction in plants, where they will apply their understanding of genetic principles to explore plant reproductive processes, reinforcing the continuity of life across different species.

lessons.title: Reproduction and inheritance
lessons.outcome: I can explain how reproduction is linked to inheritance.

lessons.title: Life cycles and reproduction
lessons.outcome: I can explain the role of reproduction as part of the life cycle of humans and other organisms.

lessons.title: Puberty in humans and sexual maturity
lessons.outcome: I can describe the changes that take place in human females and males during puberty and why these changes are necessary.

lessons.title: Gametes and fertilisation in sexual reproduction
lessons.outcome: I can describe the role of gametes and fertilisation in sexual reproduction.

lessons.title: Human reproductive organs
lessons.outcome: I can identify the organs of the human male and female reproductive system and describe the roles of the parts.

lessons.title: The human menstrual cycle
lessons.outcome: I can explain how the menstrual cycle prepares adult human females for sexual reproduction.

lessons.title: Gestation and birth in humans
lessons.outcome: I can describe the growth of a foetus and the process of giving birth.

lessons.title: Healthy pregnancy
lessons.outcome: I can name some substances that can pass through the placenta and explain the effects they have on a developing foetus.

units.title: Fuels and energetics
units.summary: This unit examines energy changes in state, exothermic and endothermic reactions, and energy transfers in various processes. It emphasises objectivity, accuracy, and precision in scientific enquiries, data interpretation, and the use of tables, graphs, and reliable methods.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Understanding chemical reactions, where they explored how substances interact and transform during reactions. It deepens their understanding by examining fuels and energetics, focusing on energy changes in chemical reactions and the impact of energy resources. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Carbon cycle and climate change, where they will apply their knowledge of fuels and energy transfers to explore the environmental impact of carbon emissions, linking chemical processes to global climate issues.

lessons.title: Heating and cooling
lessons.outcome: I can explain why some changes of state are exothermic and some are endothermic.

lessons.title: Cooling curve: practical
lessons.outcome: I can conduct an investigation to create and analyse cooling curves and identify where state changes are happening on temperature vs time graphs.

lessons.title: Exothermic and endothermic chemical reactions
lessons.outcome: I can identify whether a chemical reaction is exothermic or endothermic and explain how I know.

lessons.title: Comparing fuels
lessons.outcome: I can carry out a fair test to compare the energy transferred by burning different fuels.

lessons.title: Power stations
lessons.outcome: I can describe how burning fuels can be used to generate electricity.

lessons.title: Using renewable energy resources
lessons.outcome: I can describe how renewable energy resources can be used to generate electricity.

units.title: Making images
units.summary: This unit explores the transmission of light, including absorption, scattering, and reflection, and the use of the ray model in imaging, refraction, and lenses. It also covers energy transfer in various processes, using safe techniques, making accurate observations, and improving reliability.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Sound, light and vision, where they explored the properties of sound and light waves and how they interact with different materials. It deepens their understanding by examining how light is used to form images through reflection, refraction, and lenses. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Waves, where they will apply their knowledge of wave properties to explore the broader concepts of wave behaviour, including superposition and wave interactions, reinforcing their understanding of how waves function in various contexts.

lessons.title: Seeing in colour
lessons.outcome: I can state the primary colours of light, describe how they mix to produce other colours, and explain how the eye detects colour.

lessons.title: The visible spectrum
lessons.outcome: I can describe what white light is, and explain why a visible spectrum can be produced from white light.

lessons.title: Reflecting colour
lessons.outcome: I can explain the colour of an object in white light and in coloured light.

lessons.title: A pinhole camera
lessons.outcome: I can explain how light passes through a pinhole to produce an image in a pinhole camera.

lessons.title: Reflected images
lessons.outcome: I can describe and explain the properties of reflections in a plane mirror, and draw diagrams to show how reflections form.

lessons.title: Refracting light
lessons.outcome: I can describe and draw how a ray of light refracts when it moves from one medium to another, and explain how refraction can cause virtual images.

lessons.title: Focusing light
lessons.outcome: I can explain how light from an object can be focused by a converging lens to form an image.

units.title: Diet and exercise
units.summary: This unit covers the components of a healthy diet, energy requirements, and the effects of imbalances, exercise, asthma, and smoking on the body. It also focuses on planning scientific enquiries, applying mathematical concepts, performing calculations, and basic data analysis techniques.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Keeping healthy, where they explored the importance of a balanced diet, exercise, and lifestyle choices for overall health. It deepens their understanding by examining the specific impacts of diet and exercise on body systems, including effects of physical activity. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Disease and drugs, where they will apply their knowledge to explore how lifestyle factors contribute to disease risk and the role of drugs in managing health conditions, reinforcing the link between daily choices and long-term health.

lessons.title: Good and ill health
lessons.outcome: I can describe what is meant by physical and mental health and can identify factors and symptoms associated with ill health.

lessons.title: Balanced diet
lessons.outcome: I can describe the components of a healthy diet and how they contribute to good health.

lessons.title: Food is a source of building materials and energy
lessons.outcome: I can explain how food is used for growth and repair and to provide energy, and interpret information on food labels about the amounts of nutrients and energy provided by different foods.

lessons.title: Energy provided by food: practical
lessons.outcome: I can calculate the amount of energy provided by different foods by measuring a change in temperature.

lessons.title: Imbalanced diet: starvation and deficiency diseases
lessons.outcome: I can explain the effects on the human body of not consuming enough nutrients.

lessons.title: Imbalanced diet: obesity
lessons.outcome: I can explain the effects on the human body of consuming too much food.

lessons.title: The effects of exercise on the human body
lessons.outcome: I can describe the effects of exercise on breathing rate and heart rate, and the wider health benefits of regular exercise.

lessons.title: The effects of exercise on breathing and heart rate
lessons.outcome: I can plan and carry out an investigation into the effects of exercise on breathing rate or heart rate.

lessons.title: Recovery time after exercise
lessons.outcome: I can plot a line graph to display data on pulse rate and use it to determine a person’s recovery time after exercise.

units.title: Climate change and greenhouse gases
units.topic: Y8.14 · Climate change and greenhouse gases (Biology)
units.summary: In this unit pupils learn about greenhouse gas emissions from transport and industry, and the use of renewable energy resources and changes to transport infrastructure that could reduce emissions.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit adds to pupils’ knowledge of the greenhouse effect, global warming and climate change. It uses the contexts of transport and industry to explore some medium- and large-scale actions that lead to reductions in greenhouse gas emissions and how they can be delivered. Importantly, it develops understanding of why increasing the use of electric vehicles and electric heat pumps must be combined with an increased use of renewable energy resources for the generation of electricity, to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from transport and buildings.

lessons.title: Greenhouse gases and global warming
lessons.outcome: I can describe greenhouse gases and the effects of adding more greenhouse gases to the atmosphere.

lessons.title: Evidence for global warming
lessons.outcome: I can describe some evidence that global warming is caused by human activity

lessons.title: Impact of climate change on sea levels
lessons.outcome: I can explain how global warming can cause sea levels to rise

lessons.title: Impacts of transport on the greenhouse effect
lessons.outcome: I can compare the impact of different types of transport on global warming.

lessons.title: Reducing emissions from transport
lessons.outcome: I can describe how to travel in ways that reduce greenhouse gas emissions

lessons.title: Reducing emissions from industry
lessons.outcome: I can identify the biggest producers of carbon dioxide and suggest changes to reduce their emissions

lessons.title: Using renewable energy resources
lessons.outcome: I can describe how renewable energy resources can be used to generate electricity.

units.title: Breathing and respiration
units.summary: This unit explores the human gas exchange system, breathing mechanisms, and adaptations for function. It covers aerobic and anaerobic respiration, including fermentation, and compares their processes and implications. Focus is on accuracy, reliable measurements, and SI units.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from the Human digestive system, where they examined how nutrients are broken down and absorbed to support bodily functions. It deepens their understanding by exploring breathing and respiration, focusing on gas exchange and how oxygen is used to release energy from food. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Plant nutrition and photosynthesis, where they will apply their knowledge of respiration to understand the interdependence of respiration and photosynthesis in living organisms.

lessons.title: Breathing, respiration and gas exchange
lessons.outcome: I can describe the differences between breathing, respiration and gas exchange.

lessons.title: The human gas exchange system and breathing
lessons.outcome: I can describe how humans breathe, including the roles of different parts of the gas exchange system.

lessons.title: Estimating lung volume
lessons.outcome: I can describe how to use simple apparatus to estimate lung volume.

lessons.title: Adaptations of the human lungs for gas exchange
lessons.outcome: I can describe how the human lungs are adapted to increase the amount of gas exchange.

lessons.title: Cellular respiration
lessons.outcome: I can describe what cellular respiration is and explain why it happens in all living organisms all the time.

lessons.title: Aerobic cellular respiration
lessons.outcome: I can describe the reactants and products of aerobic cellular respiration, and where it takes place.

lessons.title: Anaerobic cellular respiration in humans
lessons.outcome: I can describe differences between aerobic and anaerobic cellular respiration in humans.

lessons.title: Anaerobic cellular respiration and fermentation in microorganisms
lessons.outcome: I can describe the reactants and products of anaerobic cellular respiration in microorganisms, and ways in which the process is useful to us.

units.title: Acids and bases
units.summary: This unit covers acids, alkalis, and their neutralisation reactions, the pH scale, and the reactions of acids with metals and alkalis. It also examines the chemical properties of metal and non-metal oxides. Emphasis is on evaluating risks, using appropriate techniques, and making observations.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Understanding chemical reactions, where they explored how substances interact and transform during chemical processes. It deepens their understanding by examining the properties of acids and bases, their reactions, and the concept of pH. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Making salts, where they will apply their knowledge of acid-base reactions to create different salts, reinforcing the practical application of chemical reactions and enhancing their understanding of chemical processes.

lessons.title: Acids and bases
lessons.outcome: I can describe some properties of acids and bases and use litmus paper to test for acids and bases.

lessons.title: pH scale and universal indicator solution
lessons.outcome: I can measure the pH of an acid or alkali using the pH scale.

lessons.title: Practical: red cabbage indicator solution
lessons.outcome: I can make red cabbage indicator solution and use it to test solutions to find out if they are acid or alkali.

lessons.title: Chemical reactions: acid and metal
lessons.outcome: I can describe what happens when an acid reacts with a metal and write word and symbol equations for these reactions.

lessons.title: Metal oxides and non-metal oxides
lessons.outcome: I can describe the properties of metal and non-metal oxides and write equations to represent reactions of metal oxides with acid.

lessons.title: Chemical reactions: neutralisation
lessons.outcome: I can describe what happens during a neutralisation reaction and write word and symbol equations to represent different neutralisation reactions.

lessons.title: Chemical reactions: acid and metal carbonate
lessons.outcome: I can describe what happens when a metal carbonate reacts with an acid and write chemical equations to describe these reactions.

units.title: Magnets and electromagnets
units.summary: This unit explores magnetism, including magnetic poles, fields, and Earth’s magnetism, along with the principles of electromagnets and DC motors. It focuses on conducting precise scientific enquiries and identifying variables and emphasises accuracy, repeatability, and reproducibility.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Series circuits, where they explored electrical components and how current flows in a simple loop. It deepens their understanding by examining the properties of magnets and electromagnets, focusing on magnetic fields and the interaction between electricity and magnetism. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Electromagnetism, where they will apply their knowledge to understand the principles behind electric motors and other electromagnetic devices, enhancing their grasp of how electricity and magnetism work together in practical applications.

lessons.title: Magnetic poles
lessons.outcome: I can describe how magnets can attract magnetic materials, as well as attract and repel other magnets.

lessons.title: The magnetic field of a bar magnet
lessons.outcome: I can plot a magnetic field around a bar magnet.

lessons.title: Electromagnets
lessons.outcome: I can describe how to make a magnet using an electric current.

lessons.title: Current through an electromagnet
lessons.outcome: I can plan an experiment to test the strength of an electromagnet and explain how different factors affect the strength of an electromagnet.

lessons.title: Using electromagets
lessons.outcome: I can describe how electromagnets are used in cranes, locks, bells and motors.

units.title: Plant nutrition and photosynthesis
units.summary: This unit covers photosynthesis, including how plants produce carbohydrates, absorb water and minerals, and the role of leaf stomata in gas exchange. It highlights the importance of photosynthesis in sustaining life on Earth and explores the adaptations of leaves for photosynthesis.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Breathing and respiration, where they explored how organisms use oxygen to release energy from food. It deepens their understanding by examining plant nutrition and photosynthesis, focusing on how plants produce their own food using light, carbon dioxide, and water. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells, where they will apply their knowledge of energy processes to understand cellular structures and functions, highlighting the differences in how cells support life across various organisms.

lessons.title: Plant nutrition
lessons.outcome: You can describe what plants need from their surroundings to stay alive and grow, and how they get food.

lessons.title: Photosynthesis
lessons.outcome: You can identify the reactants and products of photosynthesis and write a word summary of the process.

lessons.title: Adaptations of plants for photosynthesis: absorbing light
lessons.outcome: You can describe how plants are adapted to absorb light for photosynthesis.

lessons.title: Adaptations of plants for photosynthesis: gas exchange and stomata
lessons.outcome: You can describe how plants are adapted to take in and release gases to support photosynthesis.

units.title: Materials
units.summary: This unit examines the varying properties of elements, the reactivity series, and the role of carbon in metal extraction. It also explores catalysts and the properties of ceramics, polymers, and composites. Emphasis is placed on evaluating risks, using appropriate techniques, and interpreting data.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Acids and bases, where they explored chemical properties and reactions of substances. It deepens their understanding by examining different materials, including metals, polymers, and ceramics, and their properties and uses. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Using Earth's resources, where they will apply their knowledge to explore the sustainable use of natural resources, material extraction, and the environmental impact of human activity, reinforcing the link between chemistry and real-world applications.

lessons.title: Materials and composites: including metals, ceramics and polymers
lessons.outcome: I can classify materials as metals, ceramics, or polymers, and describe and predict the properties of some composite materials.

lessons.title: Structure of polymers
lessons.outcome: I can give examples of polymers and explain how the properties of polymers depend on their structure.

lessons.title: The reactivity series for metals
lessons.outcome: I can use experimental evidence to organise several metals in order of their reactivity.

lessons.title: Chemical reactions: displacement of metals
lessons.outcome: I can explain what happens when one metal displaces another metal from a salt, in solution as well as how carbon can be used to extract metals from ores.

lessons.title: Catalysts
lessons.outcome: I can describe how catalysts, including enzymes, speed up chemical reactions.

units.title: Hidden forces
units.summary: This unit explores forces, deformation, Hooke’s Law, moments, and work done. It covers pressure in liquids, atmospheric pressure, upthrust, and equilibrium, as well as simple machines and force-extension relationships, highlighting how forces affect motion, friction, and object deformation.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Forces, where they explored the basics of contact and non-contact forces and how they affect motion. It deepens their understanding by examining hidden forces, such as turning forces, forces that hold objects on surfaces, and buoyancy, highlighting how these forces interact in everyday situations. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Particle explanations of density and pressure, where they will apply their knowledge to understand how particle behaviour influences density, pressure, and the forces exerted by fluids.

lessons.title: Gravitational force and weight
lessons.outcome: I can describe and apply the relationship between mass and gravitational force.

lessons.title: Stretching springs
lessons.outcome: I can measure extensions of a spring for a good range of stretching forces.

lessons.title: Hooke's law
lessons.outcome: I can describe and explain the relationship between the extension of a spring and the force stretching it.

lessons.title: Stretching rubber
lessons.outcome: I can investigate the extension of a rubber band, and compare the behaviour to that of a spring.

lessons.title: The force of a floor
lessons.outcome: I can explain how a floor can support a range of objects with very different weights.

lessons.title: Levers
lessons.outcome: I can identify levers and describe their purpose and how they work.

lessons.title: Turning forces
lessons.outcome: I can investigate and calculate the size of turning forces.

lessons.title: Floating, mass and shape
lessons.outcome: I can explain how the density of an object determines how well it floats.

lessons.title: Pressure
lessons.outcome: I can describe and calculate pressure, the effect of a force acting over an area.

lessons.title: Pressure at different depths and heights
lessons.outcome: I can describe how the pressure changes at different depths underwater and heights in the atmosphere.

units.title: Adaptations, competition, natural selection and evolution
units.topic: Y9.07 · Adaptations, competition, natural selection and evolution (Biology)
units.summary: This unit explores variation within and between species, competition, and natural selection. It focuses on asking questions, making predictions, planning scientific enquiries, and testing hypotheses. It also covers analysing results, explaining findings, and identifying new questions that arise.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from of carbonVariation (differences within species), where they explored how genetic differences contribute to diversity within a species. It deepens their understanding by examining adaptations, competition, and natural selection, highlighting how these processes drive evolution. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Fossil evidence, selective breeding and explaining evolution, where they will apply their knowledge to study evidence for evolution, the impact of human intervention through selective breeding, and evolutionary changes.

lessons.title: Fossils show that species change over time
lessons.outcome: I can explain what fossils are and how they provide evidence that species change over time.

lessons.title: Understanding time scales
lessons.outcome: I can describe key events in the history of Earth and distinguish between billions, millions and thousands of years ago.

lessons.title: Adaptations
lessons.outcome: I can describe the adaptations of some species that make them well suited to survive in their environment.

lessons.title: Competition
lessons.outcome: I can describe resources that organisms have to compete for and explain how adaptations can be helpful.

lessons.title: Heritable variation
lessons.outcome: I can describe examples of different types of variation that can and cannot be passed on to an organism’s offspring.

lessons.title: Natural selection
lessons.outcome: I can explain how variation and competition lead to the natural selection of individuals with the most helpful characteristics.

lessons.title: A model of natural selection
lessons.outcome: I can use a model of natural selection to make predictions about how a population will change over time.

lessons.title: Evolution
lessons.outcome: I can explain the theory of evolution by natural selection.

units.title: Carbon cycle and climate change
units.topic: Y9.08 · Carbon cycle and climate change (Chemistry)
units.summary: This unit explores the rock cycle and the formation of igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks. It also examines the atmosphere's composition, human-induced carbon dioxide production, and its impact on climate. Focus is on interpreting data, identifying patterns, and presenting explanations.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Earth's resources, where they explored how natural resources are utilised and the importance of sustainable management. It deepens their understanding by examining the carbon cycle and its role in climate change, focusing on human impacts such as carbon emissions. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Atmosphere and changing climate, where they will apply their knowledge to explore the composition and evolution of Earth’s atmosphere and the ongoing impacts of climate change.

lessons.title: Physical weathering and erosion
lessons.outcome: I can describe the difference between physical weathering and erosion of rock and provide examples of each.

lessons.title: Formation of sedimentary rock
lessons.outcome: I can describe the formation of sedimentary rock and suggest information that can be obtained from its layers.

lessons.title: Fossils and the rock cycle
lessons.outcome: I can describe the formation of fossils and how the rock cycle affects our fossil record.

lessons.title: Formation of fossil fuels
lessons.outcome: I can describe what coal, oil and natural gas are, how they formed, and why they are non-renewable energy resources.

lessons.title: Gases in the atmosphere
lessons.outcome: I am able to name the main gases in the atmosphere and describe the test and some uses for each one.

lessons.title: Atmospheric carbon
lessons.outcome: I can describe how too much carbon dioxide in Earth’s atmosphere is contributing to global warming.

lessons.title: The carbon cycle
lessons.outcome: I can describe the carbon cycle and explain the effect of changes to parts of the cycle.

units.title: Waves
units.summary: This unit explores the nature of sound and water waves, including transverse and longitudinal motion, wave reflection, superposition, and the speed of sound in various media. It covers sound production, detection, and auditory ranges, emphasising data interpretation, and basic calculations.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Making images, where they explored how light interacts with materials through reflection, refraction, and the use of lenses to form images. It deepens their understanding by examining the broader properties of waves, including sound and light, and their behaviours. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Measuring waves, where they will apply their knowledge to quantify wave properties such as amplitude, wavelength, and frequency, enhancing their understanding of wave dynamics in various contexts.

lessons.title: Water waves
lessons.outcome: I can explain how water waves consist of oscillations of water and describe how water waves can superpose and reflect.

lessons.title: Sound waves
lessons.outcome: I can describe the movement of particles in a sound wave travelling through a solid, liquid or gas, and explain the relative speed of sound in each state of matter.

lessons.title: Speed of sound
lessons.outcome: I can measure the speed of sound waves in air using an echo method.

lessons.title: Hearing sound
lessons.outcome: I can explain how sound waves cause sounds to be heard, and describe the range and limits of human hearing.

lessons.title: Ultrasound
lessons.outcome: I can describe what ultrasound is and explain its properties, and also describe some uses of ultrasound.

units.title: Disease and drugs
units.summary: This unit explores the human gas exchange system, focusing on the impact of exercise, asthma, smoking, recreational drugs, and the differences between infectious and non-infectious diseases. It emphasises understanding scientific methods, evidence, risk evaluation, and peer review importance.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Diet and exercise, where they explored how lifestyle choices impact overall health and body systems. It deepens their understanding by examining the role of disease and drugs, focusing on how different conditions affect the body and the use of medications. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Health and disease, where they will apply their knowledge to explore the interactions between communicable and non-communicable diseases, lifestyle factors, and prevention strategies, reinforcing the link between health management and disease prevention.

lessons.title: Differences between infectious and non-infectious disease
lessons.outcome: I can describe some common infectious and non-infectious diseases and their causes.

lessons.title: The gas exchange system in healthy humans
lessons.outcome: I can describe the function and structures of the human gas exchange system in healthy humans.

lessons.title: Lifestyle diseases
lessons.outcome: I can describe some common lifestyle diseases, factors that increase the risk of developing them, and steps you can take to help prevent them.

lessons.title: Asthma
lessons.outcome: I can describe the symptoms of asthma, and some of the risk factors that can increase the chance of having asthma.

lessons.title: Smoking
lessons.outcome: I can describe the effects of smoking on the human body.

lessons.title: Vaping
lessons.outcome: I can explain the effects of nicotine on the body and evaluate the risks of vaping.

lessons.title: Recreational drug use: depressants
lessons.outcome: You can explain the effects of alcohol on the body in both the short and long term.

lessons.title: Recreational drug use: stimulants
lessons.outcome: I can explain how stimulants affect the body in both the short and long term.

lessons.title: Solvent abuse
lessons.outcome: I can explain what solvents are and the effects that inhaling them have on the body.

units.title: Patterns in the periodic table
units.topic: Y9.11 · Patterns in the periodic table (Chemistry)
units.summary: This unit explores the periodic table, including the principles behind Mendeleev's design, the arrangement of elements into periods and groups, and the classification of metals and non-metals. It examines how the physical and chemical properties of elements predict reaction patterns.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Atoms, elements and compounds, where they explored the basic structure of matter and how elements combine to form compounds. It deepens their understanding by examining the patterns in the periodic table, highlighting how element properties are organised based on atomic structure. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Atomic structure and the periodic table, where they will further explore how atomic configuration influences element positioning, reactivity, and trends, solidifying their grasp of chemical organisation and behaviour.

lessons.title: Groups of elements in the periodic table
lessons.outcome: I can identify and describe properties of some different groups of elements in the periodic table.

lessons.title: Group 1 and 2 metals
lessons.outcome: I can describe the pattern in the reactivity of Group 1 metals with water and Group 2 metals with dilute acid, and compare the reactivity of the two groups.

lessons.title: Group 7 (halogens)
lessons.outcome: I can describe the pattern in reactivity of Group 7 non-metals and name the products of reactions between metals and halogens.

lessons.title: Group 0 (Noble Gases)
lessons.outcome: I can describe the properties of the noble gases, their uses, and explain why they are unreactive.

units.title: Resistance and parallel circuits
units.summary: This unit covers electrical circuits, compares appliance power ratings, and understands domestic fuel use and costs. It explores electric current, potential difference, resistance, and the differences between conductors and insulators, focusing on calculations and applications in circuits.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Series circuits, where they explored current, voltage, and resistance in simple electrical loops. It deepens their understanding by examining resistance and parallel circuits, focusing on how electrical components behave differently when arranged in parallel. This prepares pupils for the next unit, Electric fields and circuit calculations, where they will apply their knowledge to explore electric fields, complex circuit behaviours, and the calculations needed to predict circuit performance, enhancing their understanding of electrical systems.

lessons.title: Electrical resistance
lessons.outcome: I can compare the electrical resistance of different components using measurements of current.

lessons.title: Thickness of a wire
lessons.outcome: I can describe how a battery pushes current through wires of different thicknesses.

lessons.title: Length of a wire
lessons.outcome: I can explain why longer wires have a higher resistance than shorter wires.

lessons.title: Making parallel circuits
lessons.outcome: I can use circuit diagrams to build parallel circuits and draw circuit diagrams of parallel circuits.

lessons.title: Voltage in parallel circuits
lessons.outcome: I can describe the rule for voltages in a parallel circuit.

lessons.title: Loops of a parallel circuit
lessons.outcome: I can divide a parallel circuit into a set of nested series circuits.

lessons.title: Measuring current in a parallel circuit
lessons.outcome: I can describe how to measure current through each branch of a parallel circuit.

lessons.title: Comparing series and parallel circuits
lessons.outcome: I can compare the properties of series and parallel circuits that have the same components.

lessons.title: Mains electricity
lessons.outcome: I can compare the power of different appliances and work out how much they cost to use.

units.title: Reproduction in plants
units.summary: This unit explores plant reproduction, including flower structure, pollination, fertilisation, seed formation, and dispersal mechanisms. It highlights the role of insect pollination in food security. Focus is on planning and conducting enquiries, and ensuring reliable observations.
units.whyThisWhyNow: This unit builds on pupils’ prior learning from Reproduction in humans, where they explored the reproductive systems and genetic inheritance in humans. It deepens their understanding by examining reproduction in plants, focusing on pollination, fertilisation, and seed formation, highlighting similarities and differences across species. This prepares pupils for the next unit, DNA and the genome, where they will apply their knowledge of reproduction to understand the molecular basis of inheritance, exploring how genetic information is stored, expressed, and passed on in all living organisms.

lessons.title: Flower structure
lessons.outcome: I can describe the function of the male and female reproductive structures in a flowering plant.

lessons.title: Pollination and fertilisation
lessons.outcome: I can describe the processes of pollination and fertilisation in flowering plants.

lessons.title: Insects and food security
lessons.outcome: I can explain the importance of insects for food security and suggest how we can protect them.

lessons.title: Fruit and seeds
lessons.outcome: I can explain how fruits are formed and how the structure of a seed enables germination.

lessons.title: Factors affecting seed germination: practical
lessons.outcome: I can plan and set up an investigation into factors affecting seed germination.

lessons.title: Factors affecting seed germination: data analysis
lessons.outcome: I can describe and explain the results of an investigation into factors affecting seed germination.

lessons.title: Seed dispersal: practical
lessons.outcome: I can explain why it is important for a plant that its seeds are dispersed over a wide area, and carry out an experiment to measure seed dispersal.

lessons.title: Seed dispersal: data analysis
lessons.outcome: I can display data as a graph or chart and identify patterns to conclude on the relationship between the independent and dependent variable.

units.title: Climate change and biodiversity
units.summary: In this unit pupils learn about the impact of agriculture and deforestation on biodiversity, and to more thoroughly consider the effects of climate change on biodiversity and food production.
units.whyThisWhyNow: The thread through this unit is agriculture, including deforestation, and its impact on biodiversity. The examples used draw on pupils’ knowledge of greenhouse gases and global warming and explore some effects of climate change in a range of contexts and in particular their impact on biodiversity and on food production. This prepares pupils for thinking about strategies to maintain biodiversity and achieve food security.

lessons.title: Agriculture and habitat loss
lessons.outcome: I can explain how growing crops for food is linked to the loss of habitats and a decrease in biodiversity.

lessons.title: Deforestation affects the carbon and water cycles
lessons.outcome: I can explain how deforestation disrupts the carbon and water cycles, and describe ways to reduce these impacts.

lessons.title: Impacts of climate change on biodiversity
lessons.outcome: I can describe impacts of climate change on biodiversity, including plants and animals.

lessons.title: Climate change and food production
lessons.outcome: I can explain how food production is affected by and contributes to climate change, and how changes in diet can help to limit climate change.

lessons.title: Advantages and disadvantages of plastic food packaging
lessons.outcome: I can describe advantages and disadvantages of plastic food packaging.
